item.text:
Yes. ResStock’s **Geometry Wall Type data for Maine are incorrect** because of mislabeled county tax assessor source data. The issue report shows an implausible single-family detached distribution of roughly **10% wood frame, 12% brick, and 78% concrete/CMU**. The report says no fix has been implemented and that all published ResStock datasets are believed to be affected. [Source: “Wall Type Issue, Especially in Maine,” corpus release `resstock_amy2018_2025_release_1-v1`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NatLabRockies/buildstock-corpus/resstock_amy2018_2025_release_1-v1/processed/resstock/resstock_amy2018_2025_release_1/github_site/docs/resources/explanations/Issue_Wall_Type_Especially_Maine.md).

The team recommends:

- **For wall type or exterior finish distributions:** use results from nearby states, especially **Vermont and New Hampshire**, as proxies.
- **For measures whose applicability depends on wall type:** reweight Maine’s results using nearby-state wall type distributions, or use nearby-state results directly. The error can undercount eligible homes for insulation measures restricted to wood-frame walls. [Official issue report and recommendations](https://natlabrockies.github.io/ResStock.github.io/docs/resources/explanations/Issue_Wall_Type_Especially_Maine.html).
